description: The >>SOURCE [FORMAT] [IS] { FIXED | FREE } compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.24) - it switches the reference format of the source or library text that follows. Implemented by LogicalLineConverter, which runs BEFORE the conditional-compilation driver (it must, to normalize the text), so the introduction gate for this ONE directive emits there rather than at the shared directive-recognition point. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.18.2 GR1: 'The SOURCE FORMAT directive indicates that the source text or library text following the directive'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 58: 'A compiler directive permits selection and intermixing of free-form or fixed-form reference format'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.19: 'directive specifies whether the reference format of the source text or library text that follows is fixed form or free form') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.24.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.24.2 general format (rendered from the printed page, folio 84): SOURCE, FIXED and FREE are underlined required words and FORMAT/IS are not, so per §2023:5.2.3 they are optional words and exactly one of FIXED or FREE shall be written; §2023:7.3.24.3 GR1 has no answer for the following text otherwise.

source:
>>SOURCE FORMAT IS FIXED
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725SF.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
